summary: Measured on the same 33 features as 13 other Belgian banks, ING scores 0.407 and reads as 'traditional, but leaning towards the challengers': it keeps traditional strengths such as a clear offer (5.0 vs 3.97) and a mobile-first layout, but it also carries the most extreme above-peer signals in the set on urgency and deadline language (4.0 vs 0.64) and persuasion techniques (5.0 vs 1.67). Its pages are also much longer and brighter than peers, and the free-account framing sits above peers on 'free' with conditions attached. No click, conversion or sales data exists in this project, so every recommendation below is a hypothesis ING can test, not a cause; the capture window is 2026-09-21 to 2026-09-23 only.

recommendations.title: Strip back urgency and deadline language
recommendations.finding: Urgency and deadline language is ING's single largest above-peer gap: 4.0 markers per page against a peer mean of 0.64, 3.69 standard deviations above the market, and it is one of the two signals furthest from the market overall. No performance data exists in this project, so the direction of the effect is untested.
recommendations.recommendation: Cut the count of deadline and scarcity phrases on account-opening and product pages to at or below the peer level, keeping at most one genuinely dated offer per page instead of stacking several. If a deadline is used, state the actual end date rather than generic pressure wording.

recommendations.title: Make the conditions of a 'free' account explicit where the claim is made
recommendations.finding: ING is above peers on "free" with conditions attached (0.67 vs a peer mean of 0.23) while nearly all traditional captures carry legal small print (0.93 of traditional pages). Conditions therefore exist but are not necessarily visible next to the claim that creates them.
recommendations.recommendation: Restate the free-account claim so the qualifying conditions (minimum deposit, salary transfer, age or package requirement, as applicable) sit in the same visual block as the claim, not only in the small print. Keep the legal small print, but stop relying on it to carry the qualification.

recommendations.title: Shorten the opening screen, not just the page
recommendations.finding: ING's pages measure 11148.67 pixels tall against a peer mean of 6411.72, and traditional pages in the set show many more elements visible without scrolling than challenger pages (36.57 vs 21.5). Long pages with dense opening screens push the offer and the next step further down.
recommendations.recommendation: Set a height budget for the top of each campaign page: one value proposition, one supporting proof point and one call to action before the first scroll. Move FAQ-style and tariff detail below the fold or to a linked detail page, and re-measure page length after the trim.

recommendations.title: Reduce the number of persuasion techniques stacked per page
recommendations.finding: ING uses 5.0 persuasion techniques per page against a peer mean of 1.67, a gap of 3.68 standard deviations, making it the joint-largest deviation from the market alongside urgency and deadline language. The analysis records the count, not the effect on behaviour.
recommendations.recommendation: Audit each campaign page and keep only the persuasion levers that support the specific offer, removing secondary ones (added pressure, social proof or bundle framing that repeats the same argument). Test one page with a single dominant argument before rolling the pattern out.

recommendations.title: Substantiate the fast sign-up promise
recommendations.finding: ING promises fast digital sign-up on 0.67 of its captures against a peer mean of 0.15, an above-peer gap of 1.42 standard deviations, and the promise sits on pages that are also the longest and densest in the set. The measurement records that the promise is made, not whether it is fulfilled.
recommendations.recommendation: Where the fast sign-up promise appears, attach a concrete, checkable description of the process (the steps required, what the customer needs at hand) next to the call to action, so the claim is anchored to the page rather than asserted on it.

recommendations.title: Put a concrete rate or price in the offer block
recommendations.finding: No traditional page in the set shows a rate, while half of the challenger pages do (0.0 vs 0.5), and challengers also frame the product in subscription style twice as often. ING's offer clarity is already high (5.0 vs 3.97), so the gap is in concreteness rather than in clarity of wording.
recommendations.recommendation: On the savings and term-account campaign pages, state the headline rate, the term and any condition in the main offer block rather than only in a tariff grid or PDF, and test a subscription-style framing ('what you get each month') against the current wording.

recommendations.title: Replace question-style headings with statements
recommendations.finding: Traditional pages in the set ask far more questions than challenger pages (20.71 vs 5.75), and ING's pages are long and information-dense. Question headings add length and read as FAQ structure rather than as an offer; the analysis records the count and no behavioural outcome.
recommendations.recommendation: Convert the question-led headings on the 'why ING', support and mortgage pages into short declarative headings that state the benefit or the answer, keeping questions only where a customer genuinely chooses between options.

recommendations.title: Hold the light, mobile-first rendering while trimming
recommendations.finding: ING is above the peer mean on page brightness (0.55 vs 0.34), is designed mobile-first on every capture (1.0 vs a peer mean of 0.56) and carries more images than peers (33 vs 19). Brighter pages and denser opening screens are the traditional signature (brightness effect size -2.36), while challengers favour a larger opening image and a higher share of the page as imagery. Brightness here is measured on a single light-mode capture; a dark-mode visitor may see something different, and three peer captures in this set were taken with a cookie banner over the page.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep the light, readable rendering and the mobile-first layout rather than adopting the darker challenger palette, and treat any change to the size of the opening image as a single isolated A/B test rather than a redesign, given that no performance data links imagery to outcomes.

recommendations.title: Only claim digital leadership the news cycle supports
recommendations.finding: Over the last 90 days ING has 2 headlines and its themes are 'other' only (2 of 2) - there is no coverage counted under innovation_digital for ING in this window, while BNP Paribas Fortis and Revolut each register 1 headline under that theme. A page that asserts fast or leading digital sign-up is making a claim the current press narrative about ING does not echo. This link is a hypothesis to verify, not a measured effect, and theme counts are topic counts, not sentiment or performance.
recommendations.recommendation: Where a page leans on a general digital-leadership or fast-sign-up framing, ground it in the concrete mechanics of ING's own process on the page instead of an unqualified leadership claim, and re-check the fit once the news window changes.
recommendations.reputation_context: ING's 90-day themes are 'other' only (2 of 2 headlines); nothing is counted under innovation_digital for ING, while BNP Paribas Fortis and Revolut each show 1 headline under that theme.

recommendations.title: Keep urgent deadline copy away from the payments-access context
recommendations.finding: One of ING's 2 headlines in the window is an 'other'-themed item about a daily transfer limit of 5,000 EUR, and the other is an 'other'-themed item about ING appearing on a JPMorgan favourites list. Placing heavy deadline or scarcity framing on account pages while that context is live is a tonal risk worth testing, not a proven effect - themes are topics only, and no page performance is measured here.
recommendations.recommendation: Review the deadline and scarcity wording on account-opening pages and prefer a plain, dated statement of the offer over generic pressure phrasing while this context is current.
recommendations.reputation_context: ING's themes are 'other' only (2 headlines), one concerning a 5,000 EUR daily transfer limit and one concerning a JPMorgan favourites listing.
